newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: No discussion of new leaders in Zimbabwe party.
newsitem.headline: No discussion of new leaders in Zimbabwe party.

text.p: Zimbabwe's ruling ZANU-PF party will not discuss leadership changes at an annual conference set for the weekend, a top party official said on Tuesday.

Speculation has been rife that the two-day conference would, among housekeeping issues, discuss who succeeds state and party President Robert Mugabe when his six-year term ends in 2002 and who takes over from his two vice-presidents.
"We will not look at any of those issues because the national people's conference has no power to do so," ZANU-PF administration secretary Didymus Mutasa told reporters.

"It has a very limited function. Power to elect new members or officers of the party resides in the congress. These issues have to wait until 1999 or until an extraordinary congress is summoned," he said.

President Mugabe, 72, and Zimbabwe's sole ruler since 1980, says ZANU-PF will settle the succession question whenever he and his two vice-presidents, Joshua Nkomo, 79, and Simon Muzenda, 74, decide to go.
Nkomo, who is ailing, announced earlier this year that he planned to retire by December but he has since kept quiet on the issue.
